explanation: This is Dickson's prime k-tuples conjecture as used by Friedlander–Luca–Stoiciu (Integers 2007; their PDF was unavailable, so I compared with Wikipedia 'Dickson's conjecture': linear forms a_i + b_i n with positive leading coefficients are simultaneously prime for infinitely many n unless a congruence condition prevents this, the condition being that for every prime p some n makes the product not divisible by p). The formal version takes k ≥ 2 forms a_i n + b_i with a_i ∈ ℕ+, b_i ∈ ℕ, n ∈ ℕ and the same local condition. Restricting b_i to be nonnegative loses nothing: any integer shifts can be made nonnegative by replacing n with n + M, which changes neither the local condition (ℕ hits every residue class) nor the infinitude. Faithful.
